output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely explained by the cooling failure on floors 6-8. One chiller was down from 4 to 19 August, and rooms ran at 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores for guests checking out 5-20 August were 6.8, and they recovered to 8.4 once the chiller was fixed. Heat accounted for 56 of the 74 negative comments, all from floors 6-8. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat. Cleanliness scores and inspection pass rates did not move, and kiosk queues and check-in scores did not move either. So I would not give notice to Orrin or pull the kiosks. The survey method was unchanged. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value scores down slightly, but that dip is within the usual August pattern, so it is unproven. I would not reverse the rate rise yet. Do not drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score; that would hide a real failure. Next steps: restore the deferred maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A return-stay offer for affected guests is reasonable, since they already got an apology and credit. Watch value scores for a few more months. I'm fairly confident in this, and I did not collect further evidence.
